title: Pauri 2, sound: hukmee hovan
hook: hukmee hovan aakaar, hukam na kahiaa jaaee
tomorrow: Pauri 2, meaning: all within the order

segments.voice: Yesterday, hukam, the order running through everything, and the wall of falsehood. Your line was walk in the order.

Some songs hook you with their first word, because they keep coming back to it. By the second verse you're singing along before you know the rest. Kids' songs do it. Protest chants do it. The second pauri of Japji does it too. Yesterday's last word, hukam, becomes today's first, and then it comes back in every line that follows, like a drum you can't stop hearing.
screen: `A CHORUS THAT STARTS THE SAME.` → `YESTERDAY'S LAST WORD.` → `TODAY'S FIRST WORD.`

segments.voice: The opening line: hukmee hovan aakaar, hukam na kahiaa jaaee. Sound it. Hukmee: HUK-mee, hukam with an ending that means by, or through: by the order. Hovan: HO-van, they come to be. Aakaar: aa-KAAR, forms, shapes. Then the second half. Hukam: the plain word again. Na kahiaa jaaee: na, not; KAH-i-aa, said; JAA-ee, can be. You can already feel it: by the order, forms come to be; the order itself can't be said. The full meaning comes tomorrow. Today, the build. The same word comes back in both halves of the next lines. Hukmee hovan jeea, hukam milai vadiaaee: by the order, living beings; by the order, greatness. Hukmee utam neech, hukam likh dukh sukh paaeeah: by the order, high and low; by the written order, sorrow and joy. A drumbeat: hukmee, hukam, hukmee, hukam. Then the pauri gathers everything up in one line with a lovely turn in its sound: hukmai andar sabh ko, baahar hukam na koe. Everyone is inside the order; outside the order, no one. Hear how andar, inside, and baahar, outside, answer each other. And the last line brings in a word you met in camp three, with seva and ego: haumai. What the pauri says about it waits for tomorrow.
screen: `HUKMEE — BY THE ORDER.` · `HUKMEE HOVAN AAKAAR.` · `THE SAME WORD IN EVERY LINE.` · `ANDAR AND BAAHAR — IN AND OUT.` · then, large: `PAURI TWO.`

segments.voice: Say the first line slowly, out loud if you can: hukmee hovan aakaar, hukam na kahiaa jaaee, three times, slower, then softer. Then, on each out-breath, just the drumbeat, hukmee, until it goes quiet and you're sitting with what your body does on its own: the heart, the breath, the small sounds. If you pray, you can rest in Waheguru.
screen: `ਹੁਕਮੀ ਹੋਵਨਿ ਆਕਾਰ ਹੁਕਮੁ ਨ ਕਹਿਆ ਜਾਈ ॥`

segments.voice: Hukam. The divine order, the command that every line of this pauri turns on, by it: hukmee, by the order.
Your line: hukmee. By the order, and nothing outside of it. Day one hundred sixty-five.

howItsDone: The second pauri of Japji, with its repeated hukmee, is recited each morning; many Sikhs know its rhythm by heart before they study its meaning.

original.note: Gurmukhi: the opening line of Japji's second pauri.

trapdoor: what you thought: a repeated word.
what it means: by the order: forms, beings, greatness, high and low, joy and sorrow all come by it.
what a scholar hears: hukmee is an instrumental form, by the order; the pauri pairs andar and baahar to say nothing stands outside it.
